record.title: Tanzanian restrictions on Kenyan truckers during May 2020 COVID border dispute
record.scope: Selective Tanzanian entry prohibition affecting Kenyan drivers/trucks, with implementation reported at multiple Kenya-facing posts.
record.crossings: Lunga Lunga/Horohoro and Taveta/Holili; retrospective KNA account also names Namanga and Isebania.
record.direction: Kenya into Tanzania for affected drivers/vehicles; outward goods could continue through transfer arrangements.
record.movement: Kenyan truck drivers and affected Kenyan-registered cargo vehicles entering Tanzania; goods transfer and some non-Kenyan-driven transit remained possible.
record.exceptions: Capital FM reports third-country transit permitted if vehicles were not driven by Kenyans; Tanzania-to-Kenya goods could be transferred at the border.
record.imposing_authority: Tanzanian regional authorities, including Tanga Regional Commissioner Martine Shidela; later bilateral transport-minister agreement.
record.enforcement: Regional directive and reported actual truck refusals; not a demonstrated nationwide all-freight ban.
record.consequences: Affected trucks refused entry; broader trade-value estimates not adopted as losses.
record.relationship: Promotes the existing unnumbered lead “Tanzanian retaliatory blockage of Kenyan cargo in May2020”. Related to H08, but distinct Tanzanian authority, direction and cargo/driver category; Kenya’s passenger closure was not ended by this agreement.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no inference of status at the 2026-10-21 cutoff.
record.official_rationale: Tanga commissioner cited preventing COVID importation. Reporting also attributes the restriction to perceived hostile treatment and Kenya’s passenger/testing measures.
record.context: Kenya’s May 16 passenger closure exempted cargo but required testing; Tanzanian regional authorities then imposed additional selective cargo-driver restrictions.
record.uncertainty: Contemporary reporting places a Holili/Taveta restriction on Sunday May 17; the separate Tanga/Horohoro directive began May 18. No synchronized onset at every post is established. May 22 is a formal bilateral framework, not observed complete restoration; local driver and registration criteria varied.

historical.duration_note: Formal change of permission; operational reopening and continuous effective duration not established. No operational interval: selective enforcement and agreement endpoint; actual full resumption not established.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Tanga commissioner directive excludes Kenyan truck drivers; later Kenyan agency account confirms dispute and selective restrictions.
May 18 is specifically the Monday Tanga directive in May 19 reporting; no synchronized onset across every crossing established.
May 22 bilateral agreement creates mutual testing and movement framework; no universal operational resumption observed.

All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Kenyan drivers, transfer of goods at border and third-country transit with non-Kenyan drivers distinguished; not all freight.
